questions.q: In a real Oracle Fusion REST error response, what does the o:errorCode field represent?
options: The invoice's currency code
An Oracle-specific application error code, useful for escalation
The HTTP method used
A random tracking number with no meaning
questions.explain: o:errorCode is an Oracle-specific code identifying the application-level error.

questions.q: Should a 400 error be retried automatically without changing anything?
options: Yes, always retry immediately
No — a 400 means the request itself is malformed, and retrying it unchanged will fail the same way
Yes, but only on Fridays
Only if the response is in XML
questions.explain: 400 errors stem from a bad request and won't resolve by retrying unchanged.

questions.q: Which status codes are generally worth retrying?
options: 404 only
429 and 5xx (server-side) errors
None — never retry anything
questions.explain: 429 (rate limit) and 5xx errors are transient and worth retrying.

options: Retrying a failed call instantly, as many times as possible
Waiting progressively longer between each retry attempt
Giving up after the first failure, always
A method for encrypting API credentials
questions.explain: Exponential backoff means increasing the wait time between retries.

questions.q: What does a 404 status code mean, and is it worth retrying?
options: The resource doesn't exist; retrying won't make it appear
The server is overloaded; always retry with backoff
Authentication succeeded; keep retrying
The request was successful
questions.explain: 404 means the resource isn't there — retrying the same request changes nothing.
